title.purpose: Page headings. The visual anchor of each page.

card-title.purpose: Section headings inside cards and dialogs.

body.purpose: Helper text, descriptions, form labels. Most on-screen text.

label.purpose: Form field labels, nav link text.

metadata.purpose: Audit log metadata. Monospace for data alignment.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Cards at rest, default buttons. Gentle presence.

shadows.name: low
shadows.purpose: Outline, secondary, destructive buttons. Subtle inputs.

shadows.name: medium
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus, select content, card hover states.

shadows.name: high
shadows.purpose: Dialog overlays. The top of the elevation stack.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.value: transition-property: color, background-color, border-color; duration: 150ms; timing: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
motion.purpose: Default state transitions for buttons, nav links, badges, inputs.

motion.name: transition-shadow
motion.purpose: Card hover lift. Shadow intensifies, not introduced from zero.

motion.name: dialog-enter
motion.value: animation: fade-in 200ms ease-out, zoom-in-95 200ms ease-out, slide-in-from-center 200ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Dialog entrance. Fade + slight zoom + slide from center.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: Skeleton loading placeholder. Gentle pulsing on muted surface.

narrative.overview:
An open, inviting surface alive with activity. Imagine a well-maintained campus bulletin board: club flyers layered with personality, event cards pinned with purpose, clear headings that draw your eye to what matters. The information is dense but never cluttered, colorful but never chaotic. Every piece earns its pushpin.

This system serves three audiences at once. Students scanning for their next club between classes need fast visual hierarchy and scannable layouts. Officers managing rosters need efficient bulk actions and unmistakable status indicators. Platform admins checking in occasionally need clear admin navigation without cluttering anyone else's view.

The visual language is Restrained in the product sense: tinted neutrals carry 90% of the surface, with the configurable brand color appearing only on primary actions, active states, and navigation identity. This restraint is strategic. Since the brand color swaps per university deployment, every element must look intentional whether the accent is navy blue, forest green, or crimson.
keyCharacteristics: Configurable accent on a slate neutral base
Cards always carry a light ambient shadow, gaining strength on hover
System font stack throughout. Hierarchy through weight and size contrast, not display fonts
Status colors (green, yellow, red) are the only fixed palette beyond neutrals
Compact density: page gaps at 24px, card padding at 16-24px, form groups at 16px

rules.name: The Configurable Accent Rule
rules.body: The brand color (--brand-primary, default #1E40AF) is the only hue that changes per deployment. Every other color is fixed. All accent usage on a given screen must trace back to var(--brand-primary) so a single env swap recolors the entire surface.

rules.name: The Size Floor Rule
rules.body: No text below 12px (0.75rem). Badge and metadata are the floor; everything else is 14px or above.

rules.name: The Always-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Cards never sit flat on the page. Even at rest, the ambient shadow separates them from the background. Hover intensifies the lift; it never introduces it from zero.

dos: Do use var(--brand-primary) for all accent-colored elements so white-label recoloring works with a single CSS variable change.
Do give cards ambient shadow at rest and medium shadow on hover. The lift is always present.
Do use status colors (green, yellow, red) consistently for membership state, RSVP response, and validation feedback.
Do keep body text at 14px (0.875rem) and above. 12px is the absolute floor for badges and metadata only.
Do use the 12px radius (rounded-xl) for cards and 6px (rounded-md) for inputs and buttons. This two-tier system is the corner vocabulary.
Do use system font stack. No custom font loading. Performance and native feel over brand typography.
Do test dark mode for every new component. All colors must work against deep night (#0f172a) and raised surface (#1e293b).
donts: Don't use emojis, illustrations, or confetti animations. Per PRODUCT.md: "This is a university tool, not a social app."
Don't create hero-metric dashboards with big numbers and gradient accents. Stats appear as inline strips beneath the greeting, not in card grids or dramatic hero layouts.
Don't use glassmorphism, gradient text (background-clip: text), or side-stripe borders (colored border-left/border-right greater than 1px).
Don't build identical card grids (same-sized icon + heading + text repeated). Cards should vary by content density and purpose.

Don't hardcode colors outside the token system. Known violations: Login/Register bg-gray-50, Register password strength colors, EventDetail RSVP button colors, Dashboard pending badge text-yellow-600.
Don't use display fonts or decorative type in UI labels, buttons, or data. System stack only.
Don't add animated page-load sequences. Per the product register: "Product loads into a task; users don't want to watch it load."
Don't use spinners for content loading states. Skeletons match the layout. Spinners only for inline button loading indicators.
